works.title: Goldberg Variations
works.overview: An aria frames thirty variations, transforming a single bass pattern into dances, canons and intricate musical conversations. Written for a two-manual harpsichord, the work is also a cornerstone of the piano repertoire. Listen for the opening aria’s quiet return after the final variation.

works.title: Brandenburg Concertos
works.overview: Six concertos bring together strikingly different combinations of instruments. Bach lets individual players step out of the ensemble, then folds them back into the conversation. Each concerto has its own character, from brilliant brass to the intimate sound of strings.

works.title: The Well-Tempered Clavier
works.overview: Two books of preludes and fugues explore every major and minor key. The preludes range from flowing simplicity to virtuoso invention; the fugues build intricate conversations from a single theme. Listen to a pair on its own or follow a whole book’s changing landscape.

works.title: St Matthew Passion
works.overview: Bach tells the Passion story through narration, dramatic choruses, reflective arias and chorales. Two choirs and two instrumental ensembles create an extraordinary sense of space. The individual arias pause the unfolding drama and invite the listener into its emotional world.

works.title: Cello Suites
works.overview: Six suites turn one unaccompanied cello into a complete musical world. Each begins with a prelude and continues through a sequence of dances. The familiar opening of the First Suite offers a gentle starting point; the later suites explore darker colours and greater technical demands.

works.title: Toccata and Fugue in D Minor
works.overview: A dramatic opening, sweeping runs and a powerful fugue make this one of the most recognisable works associated with Bach. The contrast between free, improvisatory passages and tightly organised counterpoint is central to its appeal. Its authorship has been debated by scholars.

works.title: Requiem in D Minor
works.overview: Dark orchestral colours, urgent choral writing and moments of tender reflection shape Mozart’s final, unfinished work. The familiar completion by Franz Xaver Süssmayr carries it through the closing movements. Different recordings may use different completions, making the choice of performance especially revealing.

works.title: Symphony No. 40
works.overview: Restless energy runs through this G-minor symphony, beginning with its immediately recognisable opening theme. Four movements balance urgency, elegance and contrapuntal complexity. Notice how the quiet beginning builds tension without the ceremonial introduction of many other symphonies.

works.title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik
works.overview: This serenade for strings opens with a bold flourish and moves through a lyrical Romanze, a minuet and an energetic finale. Its clear textures make it an inviting introduction to Mozart’s instrumental writing. Compare the intimacy of a small ensemble with the breadth of a string orchestra.

works.title: Der Hölle Rache
works.overview: The Queen of the Night’s second aria in The Magic Flute turns fury into a dazzling display of vocal agility. Its repeated high notes and sharply articulated runs demand extraordinary control from the soprano. Hear it on its own, then explore its place in the opera’s drama.

works.title: Symphony No. 9
works.overview: Beethoven’s final symphony travels from a mysterious opening through a propulsive scherzo and expansive slow movement to its choral finale. Voices enter with Schiller’s Ode to Joy, giving the work an entirely new scale. Hear the four movements together to follow its dramatic journey.

works.title: Symphony No. 5
works.overview: Four opening notes become the driving force of an entire symphony. Beethoven develops that short idea through tension, lyricism and rhythmic insistence, leading from C minor to a triumphant C-major finale. The transition between the third and fourth movements is one of its defining moments.

works.title: Piano Sonata No. 14 “Moonlight”
works.overview: The familiar, hushed first movement is only the beginning. A brief, lighter middle movement leads to a turbulent finale, revealing the sonata’s dramatic range. Beethoven described the work as a sonata ‘quasi una fantasia’; the Moonlight nickname came later.

works.title: String Quartet No. 14
works.overview: Seven connected movements form a continuous journey, beginning with a searching fugue. Beethoven moves between profound stillness, dance, variation and driving energy. Following the whole quartet reveals how its contrasting episodes belong to a single, deeply connected design.

works.title: Nocturnes
works.overview: Chopin’s nocturnes turn the piano into a singing voice. A lyrical melody floats above a flowing accompaniment, often interrupted by a more turbulent central passage. The collection spans much of his creative life, from the familiar early pieces to the subtle harmonic language of the late nocturnes.

works.title: Ballade No. 1
works.overview: A single movement unfolds with the breadth of a musical narrative. Reflective passages, singing themes and mounting virtuosity lead to a fierce coda. Rather than illustrating a fixed story, the ballade invites the listener to follow its changing emotional and harmonic direction.

works.title: 24 Préludes
works.overview: Twenty-four miniature worlds move through every major and minor key. Some last only moments; others unfold as complete dramas. Heard as a sequence, the sharply contrasting moods create a remarkable arc. The longer D-flat-major prelude is commonly known as the Raindrop.

works.title: Swan Lake
works.overview: A recurring swan theme links the ballet’s lyrical scenes and dramatic confrontations. Tchaikovsky’s score balances intimate solos with elaborate dances and powerful orchestral climaxes. A complete recording follows the story in detail; a suite offers a shorter introduction to its best-known music.

works.title: Symphony No. 6 “Pathétique”
works.overview: An intensely personal symphony moves from an expansive first movement through an unusual five-beat waltz and a forceful march. Its final movement then turns inward, ending in a slow, fading lament. The contrast between apparent triumph and the closing pages gives the work its extraordinary power.

works.title: Suite bergamasque
works.overview: Four piano movements combine dance-inspired writing with Debussy’s distinctive harmonic colour. The gentle Clair de lune sits between a minuet and a lively passepied. Listening to the complete suite places that familiar movement in a richer, more varied musical setting.

works.title: La mer
works.overview: Three symphonic sketches evoke the sea through constantly changing orchestral colours. Rather than a literal soundtrack, the music suggests motion, light and the shifting relationship between wind and water. Listen for ideas that return transformed as the work unfolds.

works.title: The Four Seasons
works.overview: Four violin concertos follow spring, summer, autumn and winter. Birdsong, storms, dances and icy landscapes emerge from vivid instrumental gestures. Each concerto has three movements, offering an easy way to compare the atmosphere of the seasons or explore the whole cycle.

works.title: Piano Concerto No. 2
works.overview: Bell-like piano chords open a concerto famous for its expansive melodies and rich orchestral sound. Three movements move from dark intensity through lyrical stillness to a brilliant finale. The soloist is woven into the orchestral texture as often as it steps into the foreground.

works.title: Vocalise
works.overview: A wordless melody carries the expressive weight of this song. Originally written for high voice and piano, Vocalise has also become familiar in instrumental and orchestral arrangements. The different versions offer a revealing comparison of how phrasing and tone can shape the same musical line.
